did_you_know.text: In ancient Egypt, frogs were associated with fertility and the goddess Heqet, so the plague turned a familiar symbol into a frightening nuisance.
The magicians can imitate the appearance of the frogs, but later they cannot produce lice or stop the plagues.
The phrase “Glory over me” means here, “Choose the time.” Moses lets Pharaoh decide when the plague will end.
The word “heaps” describes large piles, not just a few dead frogs. That is why the text also mentions a foul smell spreading through the land.
The exact meaning of the biblical word kinim is uncertain; it may refer to lice, gnats, or other tiny insects.
“The finger of God” is a figurative expression for divine power revealed in an act, not a literal finger.
The identity of the arov is not completely certain. The word may describe a mixture of animals or harmful creatures, so translations differ.
Goshen is usually identified with a fertile area in the eastern Nile Delta, although its exact boundaries are unknown.
The chapter repeats a pattern of promises during trouble followed by withdrawal after relief. It raises the question of whether real change is measured by words or actions.
